note: The same six options and defaults, as booleans.
Forge's own ECMA-48 pattern: CSI, OSC/DCS/SOS/PM/APC strings and two-byte ESC sequences.
Starts with a lower case letter and counts letters only, as CyberChef does; adds a first parameter to start upper.
Only letters with a case are varied (at most 12, so at most 4,096 lines) instead of every character; the first letter varies fastest, all lower case first; the delimiter is a choice.
Forge's own pattern tokenizer: letters become [xX] (the letter as written first), classes and ASCII letter ranges gain the other case, escapes, group names and quantifiers are copied.
The exact inverse of case:to-insensitive-regex (a class with both cases of a letter becomes the first one); CyberChef's own pattern shapes are not reproduced.
The delimiter is the shared choice list (a space by default), a backwards range is E_RANGE, ranges may not exceed 65,536 code points, and \- and \\ are the only escapes.
Named remove (drop is a core word).

Forge's own escaper, written in FL (CyberChef uses a library): levels special, everything and minimal; quote single, double or backtick; JSON, ES6 and upper-case hex options; no surrounding quotes; NUL is \x00; everything uses numeric escapes only.
Reads the single-letter escapes, \xHH, \uHHHH (and surrogate pairs), \u{H} and octal; an unknown escape is kept as written.
Modes string and regex plus an ignore-case flag; CyberChef's extended-string mode (\n, \x escapes in the search text) is not offered, use string-escape:unescape on the pattern.
Units byte and bit as CyberChef, plus char; input raw or hex.
Over code points; the dynamic programme is a private primitive (limit 100 million cells).

A text report instead of highlighted HTML: one row per matching line with a score, the matched positions and the line, scored by a documented greedy rule rather than CyberChef's Sublime-style matcher.
A text report instead of highlighting: one row per stretch of offsets where all samples share the same character (offset, length, text).
